title: Information management and decision-making in child and adolescent mental health services in a low-resource healthcare setting
journal: Journal of Health Organization and Management
abstract: Purpose Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS) in low-resource healthcare settings face workforce shortages, structural barriers and fragmented information systems. Little is known about how CAMHS professionals use information to support operational and tactical decision-making. This study describes how CAMHS professionals manage and use information to support decision-making in a low-resource CAMHS setting. Design/methodology/approach A descriptive qualitative study was conducted using two in-person focus group discussions with 17 CAMHS professionals. Participants were selected through purposive sampling, and data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. The interview guide was informed by the Descriptive Model of Decision-Making Levels and Information Management in Hospitals. Findings were discussed in relation to the World Health Organization's Global Strategy on Digital Health (2020–2025). Findings The analysis developed three themes: (1) foundational conditions shaping information-driven decision-making in CAMHS; (2) workforce capacity and role-specific health information system (HIS) use; and (3) alignment between HIS and real-world care delivery and decision-making. Strengthening information-driven decision-making in CAMHS requires reliable infrastructure, system-level governance, role-specific workforce capacity building and people-centred system design. Informal practices, such as verbal follow-up, printed records, spreadsheets and messaging platforms, played an important role in maintaining information flow when formal systems were incomplete, inaccessible or poorly aligned with daily work. Originality/value This study is among the first to explore how CAMHS professionals manage and use information in a low-resource CAMHS setting. It offers insight into how infrastructure, governance, workforce capacity, informal practice and system design shape operational and tactical decision-making. These insights can inform context-appropriate information systems and information governance strategies.
